bands.label: First moves
bands.description: A gentle starting point while you learn how the pieces move. Expect simple plans, missed threats, and chances to try things out.
bands.focus: Get comfortable moving pieces and spotting captures.
bands.guidance: Play like a new learner: use simple one-move plans, sometimes overlook threats or leave pieces unprotected, and avoid deep combinations. Do not consistently choose the strongest move.

bands.label: Finding your feet
bands.description: A relaxed challenge with more purposeful moves. Gemini looks for obvious captures but can still miss a fork or leave an opening.
bands.focus: Protect your pieces and notice your opponent’s threats.
bands.guidance: Use basic development and obvious captures. Notice immediate threats, but sometimes miss forks, combinations, or positional weaknesses. Keep plans short and allow occasional natural inaccuracies.

bands.label: Club practice
bands.description: A balanced opponent that develops pieces, protects its king, and spots simple tactics. Good for practicing a plan a few moves ahead.
bands.focus: Look for forks, pins, and a plan for your next few moves.
bands.guidance: Choose sound intermediate-level moves: develop pieces, keep your king safe, avoid hanging material, and look for simple tactics. Consider short sequences, with occasional positional inaccuracies.

bands.label: Tactical challenge
bands.tagline: Give your next move a second look.
bands.description: A sharper opponent that looks for combinations and puts loose pieces under pressure. You’ll need to check what your opponent can do in reply.
bands.focus: Calculate replies and turn small advantages into a plan.
bands.guidance: Calculate forcing checks, captures, threats, and the opponent's best replies several moves ahead. Seek tactical combinations and exploit loose pieces. Maintain sound positional play and avoid simple blunders.

bands.label: Stretch yourself
bands.description: The most demanding setting: Gemini aims for careful calculation and patient positional play, giving you fewer easy opportunities.
bands.focus: Anticipate plans, calculate carefully, and practice endgames.
bands.guidance: Aim for your strongest play. Compare candidate moves using concrete calculation of forcing lines and best defensive replies. Consider king safety, pawn structure, long-term plans, prophylaxis, and endgame technique. Avoid deliberate mistakes.
